#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Remove build artifacts older than the retention window.

set -uo pipefail

readonly DEFAULT_DAYS=14

main() {
  local dir="${1:-artifacts}"
  local days="${2:-${DEFAULT_DAYS}}"

  if [[ -d ${dir} ]]; then
    find "${dir}" -type f -name '*.tar.gz' -mtime "+${days}" -delete
  fi

  printf 'pruned %s (older than %s days)\n' "${dir}" "${days}"
}

main "$@"

content.content:
# artifact-retention

`bin/prune-artifacts.sh [DIRECTORY] [DAYS]` deletes build artifacts older than the
retention window. It runs from cron on the artifact host:

```text
30 4 * * * /opt/retention/bin/prune-artifacts.sh /srv/artifacts 14
```

There are no automated tests in this repository.

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Behavior checks for bin/prune-artifacts.sh. Run: tests/prune-artifacts.test.sh

set -uo pipefail

script="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/.." && pwd)/bin/prune-artifacts.sh"
tmp="$(mktemp -d)"
trap 'rm -rf "${tmp}"' EXIT
failures=0

check() {
  local name="$1" ok="$2"
  if [[ ${ok} == 1 ]]; then printf 'ok   %s\n' "${name}"; else printf 'FAIL %s\n' "${name}"; failures=$((failures + 1)); fi
}

# Missing directory: nonzero exit, error on stderr, no "pruned" success message.
out="$("${script}" "${tmp}/missing" 14 2>"${tmp}/err")"; rc=$?
check "missing dir exits nonzero" $((rc != 0))
check "missing dir names path on stderr" $(grep -qF "${tmp}/missing" "${tmp}/err" && echo 1 || echo 0)
check "missing dir prints no success message" $([[ -z ${out} ]] && echo 1 || echo 0)

# Existing directory: old archives removed, new kept, exit 0.
mkdir "${tmp}/art"
touch -d '30 days ago' "${tmp}/art/old.tar.gz"
touch "${tmp}/art/new.tar.gz"
out="$("${script}" "${tmp}/art" 14)"; rc=$?
check "existing dir exits 0" $((rc == 0))
check "old archive removed" $([[ ! -e ${tmp}/art/old.tar.gz ]] && echo 1 || echo 0)
check "new archive kept" $([[ -e ${tmp}/art/new.tar.gz ]] && echo 1 || echo 0)

# Empty existing directory is still a success.
mkdir "${tmp}/empty"
"${script}" "${tmp}/empty" 14 >/dev/null; rc=$?
check "empty dir exits 0" $((rc == 0))

exit $((failures > 0))
E
chmod +x tests/prune-artifacts.test.sh; tests/prune-artifacts.test.sh; echo rc=$?
git stash -q -- bin; echo "--- against old script"; tests/prune-artifacts.test.sh; echo rc=$?; git stash pop -q; git status --short

content.text:
`bin/prune-artifacts.sh` now fails loudly when the directory doesn't exist. I haven't committed anything.

- **Missing directory:** it prints `prune-artifacts: directory not found: <path>` to stderr and exits 1. It no longer prints the "pruned …" success line. Cron will now report the failure.
- **`find` errors:** a failure inside `find` now also makes the script exit nonzero. Before, it would have printed "pruned" regardless.

I added `tests/prune-artifacts.test.sh`, which uses temp directories. It covers these cases:
- A missing directory exits nonzero, names the path on stderr, and prints no success message.
- An existing directory exits 0, deletes the old archive and keeps the new one.
- An empty directory exits 0.

All 7 checks pass with the fix. I also stashed the script change and re-ran the tests against the original script. The three missing-directory checks failed there and the other four passed, so the tests do detect the bug.

I also replaced the README line saying there are no tests with a note about the new exit behavior and the test script.

If you deploy this change, the first cron run with a bad path will now fail instead of passing silently. If your cron setup doesn't send mail or alert on failures, you'll still need that for the failure to be noticed.
